category: free premium-link generator with a 220-host landing list

free_tier.stated: 'Download from 220+ file hosting sites at maximum speed today' and 'Bypass slow downloads and paywalls'. No cap, no trial, no price is stated anywhere on the page.
free_tier.notes: An 'unlimited' claim with no stated counter; the only way to find the real cap is to generate links until it stops.

egress.terms: No bandwidth, quota or pricing language on the page at all; the only claim is 'maximum speed'.

interface_detail: A host picker ('Select a filehost to leech from') leading to one page per host (/premium-generator/<host>); no API, CLI or plugin documented.
chaining: Its value is the per-host landing pages rather than the service: they are SEO pages that name a host, which makes the site a usable host index even if the generator does not work.
limits_note: No limit is published, which for a free service usually means an undocumented per-IP cap; nothing was measured.
binding_note: Inferred, not documented: a free generator that publishes no account quota is almost always shaped per IP, and the site states no counter of any other kind. The inference is recorded as an inference.

identity_cost.detail: No login, no account and no email field appears on the generator page; the host picker is usable directly.

reliability_note: The 220-host list is padded with hosts that no longer exist, so the effective coverage is well below the headline (see notes). No status page.
confidence_note: The 220+ claim, the host list and the absence of any counter are read from the vendor page. The binding is inferred. A generated link would show whether the service works at all; the dead-host finding is measured separately.

evidence.proved: the '220+' host claim and the full host list, which includes zippyshare.com, anonfiles.com, netload.in, uploaded.net and rapidshare.io
that one host on the list is dead, by the host's own memorial page: 'Here lies Zippyshare [2006 - 2023]' and 'Farewell.'

notes: The 220-host figure is the weakest claim: the list still carries Zippyshare (whose own front page announces its 2023 death), anonfiles.com, netload.in and rapidshare.io, so a reader who counts hosts is counting graves. The generator itself was not exercised, so the service may be fine; what is refuted is the coverage number, not the service.
